Corrections and Updates Testimony of the Gas Rate Design Panel 
 
Page 1 of 12 
Q. 
Please identify the members of the Gas Rate Design Panel. 
1 
A. 
The Gas Rate Design Panel (“Panel”) consists of Kellie I. Smith, Melissa M. 
2 
Barnes, and Howard S. Gorman.  This is the same Panel that submitted direct 
3 
testimony as part of Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation d/b/a National Grid’s 
4 
(“Niagara Mohawk” or the “Company”) July 31, 2020 filing.  The terms defined 
5 
in the Panel’s direct testimony have the same meanings here. 
6 
 
7 
Q. 
What is the purpose of the Panel’s corrections and updates testimony? 
8 
A. 
The Panel provides corrections and updates to Niagara Mohawk’s revenue 
9 
forecast, Embedded Cost of Service Study (“ECOSS”), revenue allocation, rate 
10 
design, Merchant Function Charge (“MFC”), Revenue Decoupling Mechanism 
11 
(“RDM”) annual targets, Earnings Adjustment Mechanism (“EAM”) 
12 
allocators, and Marginal Cost of Service Study (“MCS”) based on corrections 
13 
and updates to the sales forecast and revenue requirement changes identified 
14 
since the July 31, 2020 filing.  The Panel also provides revised bill impacts 
15 
based on the corrected and updated information.  Finally, the Panel updates 
16 
certain tariff fees, load factor ratios, and the daily balancing service demand 
17 
charge.   
18 
 
19 
Q. 
Has the Panel prepared any exhibits to reflect its corrections and updates? 
20 
A. 
Yes.  The Panel prepared the following exhibits and one appendix.   
21

Q. 
In this testimony, will the Panel refer to any information provided during 
7

11 
Q.  
Please describe the updates to Exhibit __ (G-RDP-2CU), Schedule 1. 
12 
A.  
Exhibit __ (G-RDP-2CU), Schedule 1 shows the Company’s total forecast Rate 
13 
Year revenues of $611.1 million based on current rates and current surcharges.  
14 
The revenue forecast as shown on Exhibit __ (G-RDP-2CU), Schedule 1 
15 
updates base delivery revenues, MFC revenue, commodity revenue, and GRT 
16 
as a result of the Company’s update to its sales forecast as described in the 
17 
corrections and updates testimony of Company Witness Theodore E. Poe, Jr.  
18 
While Exhibit __ (G-RDP-2CU) still includes estimated ESCO commodity 
19 
revenue for illustrative purposes, that revenue is no longer included in the total 
20 
revenue column in the exhibit.  The base delivery rates for SC 6 were also 
21 


--- Page 5 ---
Corrections and Updates Testimony of the Gas Rate Design Panel 
 
Page 4 of 12 
updated to reflect the most current rates.  In addition, (i) LPC revenues were 
1 
updated to reflect the change in retail revenues, (ii) supervision and 
2 
administration revenues and miscellaneous third-party revenues were updated 
3 
to reflect the change in the general inflation rate, and (iii) Geothermal and 
4 
Hydrogen revenues were updated to reflect the changes as discussed in the 
5 
corrections and updates testimony of the Future of Heat Panel. 
6 
 
7 
Q.  
Please describe the updates to Exhibit __ (G-RDP-3CU). 
8 
A. 
Exhibit __ (G-RDP-3CU) presents an updated ECOSS (“ECOSS (CU)”) to 
9 
reflect the revenue requirement presented in Exhibit __ (RRP-1CU), as well as 
10 
the sales forecast and customer count presented in Exhibit __ (G-RDP-2CU).  
11 
The ECOSS (CU) corrects the allocation of Information, Demonstration, and 
12 
Selling Expenses (which includes credit card fees) (accounts 912-16) to allocate 
13 
those costs based on number of customers, as discussed in the Company’s 
14 
response to Information Request No. MI-018, and refines the allocation of costs 
15 
in Customer Assistance Expense (account 908) to reflect the programs in that 
16 
account (see Exhibit __ (G-RDP-3CU), Schedule 9I).  There were no changes 
17 
to the methodology from the Company’s initial ECOSS filed July 31, 2020, and 
18 
no other changes in the assignment or developer allocators. 
19 
 
20 


--- Page 6 ---
Corrections and Updates Testimony of the Gas Rate Design Panel 
 
Page 5 of 12 
The results of the ECOSS (CU) are presented on Exhibit __ (G-RDP-3CU), 
1 
Schedule 1.  Lines 1-11 show delivery revenue at present rates, net income at 
2 
present rates, rate base, and rate of return on rate base, for the total Company 
3 
and for each rate class.  Line 10 presents the return on rate base at present rate 
4 
revenue for each class and line 11 compares each class’s return to the system 
5 
return of 4.61 percent.  Line 12 presents the revenue requirement for each class 
6 
to achieve the system average target return of 6.31 percent, and line 26 
7 
computes the change in base delivery revenues needed to achieve this revenue 
8 
requirement. This information provides guidance for allocation of the 
9 
Company’s proposed revenue increase and rate design.  
10 
 
11 
Q.  
Please describe the Company’s updated proposed revenue allocation as 
12 
shown in Exhibit __ (G-RDP-4CU). 
13 
A. 
Exhibit __ (G-RDP-4CU), Schedule 1 presents the proposed revenue allocation 
14 
to meet the revenue requirement presented in Exhibit __ (RRP-1CU).  To 
15 
produce the target revenue for each class, the Panel multiplied by 87.03 percent 
16 
the proposed increases in the originally filed Exhibit ___ (G-RDP-4), Schedule 
17 
1, line 35; the updated proposed increases are shown on Exhibit __ (G-RDP-
18 
4CU), Schedule 1, line 35.  This was appropriate because the relative returns 
19 
for each class computed in the ECOSS (CU) were reasonably close to the 
20 
relative returns in the Company’s initial filing (compare Exhibit __ (G-RDP-
21 


--- Page 7 ---
Corrections and Updates Testimony of the Gas Rate Design Panel 
 
Page 6 of 12 
4CU), Schedule 1, line 8 to Exhibit __ (G-RDP-4), Schedule 1, line 8, and the 
1 
position of each class with respect to the average return and the tolerance band 
2 
was also similar to the initial filing). 
3 
 
4 
The delivery revenue proposed for each class is shown on Exhibit __ (G-RDP-
5 
4CU), Schedule 1, line 37. 
6 
 
7 
Q. 
How were the proposed rates for each class developed? 
8 
A. 
Exhibit __ (G-RDP-4CU), Schedule 3A presents the proposed rates for each 
9 
class.  The proposed rates produce the target revenue for each class that is 
10 
developed on Schedule 1, line 37 with very small differences due to rounding.  
11 
The proposed fixed monthly charges are the same as in the Panel’s initial filing, 
12 
representing small increases for most classes.  The volumetric rates were 
13 
increased to produce the balance of the revenue target for each class.  For SC-
14 
1 and SC-2, the tail block rates were increased by a greater percentage than the 
15 
mid-block rates to promote conservation. 
16 
  
17

4 
Q.  
Please describe the updates to Exhibit __ (G-RDP-9CU). 
5 
A.  
Exhibit___(G-RDP-9CU), Schedule 1 updates the paperless billing credit 
6 
calculation as a result of the change in the general inflation rate.  Although the 
7 
general inflation rate has changed, the paperless bill credit calculation did not 
8 
change.  Therefore, the Company is not proposing to modify the paperless bill 
9 
credit of $0.40 in its July 31, 2020 filing.   
10 
 
11 
Exhibit __ (G-RDP-9CU), Schedule 3 updates the Company’s calculation of its 
12 
one-bill billing charge to ESCOs for consolidated billing.  Although the 
13 
calculation shows a billing charge of $0.81, the Company proposes to maintain 
14 
the proposed $0.80 billing charge to an ESCO that supplies gas to a gas-only 
15 
customer and $0.40 to an ESCO that supplies gas to a dual gas and electric 
16 
customer submitted in its July 31, 2020 filing.  By doing so, the ESCO billing 
17 
charge and customer backout credit will be consistent regardless of whether the 
18 
customer is a gas-only customer or a dual gas and electric customer. 
19

NIAGARA MOHAWK POWER CORPORATION d/b/a NATIONAL GRID 
Case Nos. 20-E-0380 and 20-G-0381 
Electric and Gas Rates 
Request for Information 
FROM: 
Multiple Intervenors, Michael B. Mager 
TO: 
National Grid 
SUBJECT:   Credit Card Fees
Request: 
18.
Explain how credit card fees are allocated to electric and gas service classes under the
Company’s embedded cost of service studies.
Response:  
For both Electric and Gas, credit card fees are included in Customer Service - Miscellaneous 
Expenses (account 910).  Credit card fees are not usually broken out and allocated separately in an 
embedded cost study. 
For Electric, this account is allocated based on number of customers. 
For Gas, this account was allocated based on firm deliveries in the initial filing.  The Company 
will revise the allocation of credit card fees to be based on number of customers in the Corrections 
and Updates filing.

Howard Gorman
